title: Countable models: three order patterns and the impossibility of two
summary: Classify the three countable models of a named dense order, then prove that a complete countable-language theory cannot have exactly two countable models.
abstract: Name an increasing sequence in a dense order. There may be nothing above all its terms, there may be a first upper bound, or there may be upper bounds with no first one. We show that these three possibilities classify the countable models of one complete theory, although no first-order sentence distinguishes them. Could a different complete theory have exactly two countable models? The answer is no. Using the earlier constructions of atomic and saturated models, we build a third model whenever a complete theory in a countable language has an infinite model and was supposed to have exactly two. The named-order example shows why three really is possible.
